subject: chemistry
title: Measurement & Data Processing Adventure 2: IR, mass and ¹H NMR spectroscopy
welcome_lead: Today you'll identify molecules with IR, MS and NMR.
meta_desc: Chemistry — IR fingerprints, mass spec fragmentation, ¹H NMR chemical shifts and splitting.
final_note: You learned IR identifies functional groups (O-H, C=O), MS shows fragments + M⁺, ¹H NMR gives chemical shifts and integration of H environments.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Bonds absorb IR at characteristic frequencies (related to mass + bond strength).

Key absorptions:
- O-H (alcohol): 3200-3550 cm⁻¹, broad.
- O-H (carboxylic acid): 2500-3300 cm⁻¹, very broad.
- N-H: 3300-3500.
- C=O: 1700-1750.
- C=C: 1620-1680.

Fingerprint region (<1500): unique pattern per molecule.

Molecular ion M⁺ gives molecular Mr (highest m/z peak typically).

Fragments come from breaking bonds. Common losses:
- m/z -15: loss of CH₃.
- m/z -17: loss of OH.
- m/z -29: loss of CHO or C₂H₅.
- m/z -45: loss of COOH.

Useful for matching to databases.

Each H environment gives one peak (chemical shift δ ppm vs TMS).

- 0.5-1.5: alkyl CH
- 2-3: next to C=O or aromatic
- 3.5-4.5: next to O
- 6.5-8: aromatic H
- 9-10: -CHO
- 10-12: -COOH

Integration shows ratio of H atoms.
Splitting (n+1 rule): coupling to n neighbouring Hs.

HL: NMR is now medical (MRI) — same principle, no harmful radiation.

What does the M+ peak in a mass spectrum represent?
options: The M+ peak shows the mass of the largest fragment after the molecule breaks apart.
The M+ peak shows the mass of a single hydrogen atom added to the molecule.
The molecular ion — formed when a single electron is removed from the whole molecule, giving the relative molecular mass.
Chemical shift is the mass of the molecule divided by 1000.

mcqs.q: What does an NMR chemical shift (δ, in ppm) actually measure?
options: Chemical shift is the mass of the molecule divided by 1000.
Chemical shift is the absolute resonance frequency of the nucleus in Hz.
The M+ peak shows the mass of a single hydrogen atom added to the molecule.
The position of a peak RELATIVE to TMS (tetramethylsilane, δ = 0), normalised by the spectrometer frequency.

mcqs.q: What is the role of the fingerprint region (below ~1500 cm^-1) in IR spectroscopy?
options: The fingerprint region is the part that contains all the most useful absorptions.
It is unique to each compound — used to identify a specific molecule by matching to a known spectrum.
The fingerprint region is used to identify which functional groups are present.
Chemical shift is the mass of the molecule divided by 1000.
